input.quote: This Agreement will automatically renew for additional 1-year terms unless earlier terminated pursuant to this Agreement's express provisions (together with the Initial Term, such additional periods the "Term"). Neither Party may terminate this Agreement during the Initial Term except as set forth in paragraph 4(b) or any Exhibit. Either Party may terminate this Agreement for any reason following the Initial Term upon ninety (90) days written notice to the other Party.
input.rationale: The Agreement auto-renews for 1-year terms (renewal length is fine and no uncapped price uplift language appears, which we simply note), but the only exit mechanic after the Initial Term requires ninety (90) days' written notice. That exceeds the fallback ceiling of a 60-day non-renewal window and sits at the walk-away boundary, so it fails on a material term. We propose the preferred 30-day opt-out for Customer while leaving Kubient's 90-day notice untouched; a 60-day Customer window is our fallback.

ops.oldText: Either Party may terminate this Agreement for any reason following the Initial Term upon ninety (90) days written notice to the other Party.
ops.newText: Customer may terminate this Agreement, or elect not to renew any renewal term, for any reason following the Initial Term upon thirty (30) days written notice to Kubient, and Kubient may terminate this Agreement for any reason following the Initial Term upon ninety (90) days written notice to Customer.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We shortened our exit/non-renewal window on the automatic 1-year renewals to thirty (30) days, consistent with our playbook position that renewals must be easy to exit (sixty (60) days is our fallback); Kubient's ninety (90) day notice right is unchanged.
proposal.summary: Reduce Customer's non-renewal/termination notice window after the Initial Term from 90 to 30 days.
